 Judgment

1) By way of present revision application under Sections 397 read with 401 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant - original accused have prayed for quashing and setting aside the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 30.04.1999 in Criminal Case No.1603 of 1995, passed by the learned 2nd Joint Civil Judge & JMFC, Amreli, by which the applicant was convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 2(1a)(a), 2(1a)(m), 7(1) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (which shall hereinafter be referred to as "Act" for short) and sentenced for a period of six months of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/560/2009

JUDGMENT DATED: 18/03/2026 undefined simple Ibrahimbhai Kalabhai vs State Of Gujarat on 18 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61055261/
1 imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/- (One Thousand), and in default to undergo further one month simple imprisonment.

sentences.text:
The said order was assailed by way of filing Criminal Appeal No.7 of 1999,
wherein, vide judgment dated 31.08.2009 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Amreli, the appeal came to be dismissed and the order of the trial Court has been confirmed and upheld in the appeal.
Hence, the present Revision Application is filed by the applicants-accused.

2) Learned Advocate for the applicant has submitted that both the Courts have committed error in convicting the applicant as the evidence is not properly appreciated more particularly failed to consider the evidence produced by the Food Inspector at Exhibit 29 and helper at Exhibit 62, both the evidence are self contrary evidence and they have committed error in taking the sample of ice candy (kulfi) and the evidence of collection of sample is not trustworthy.
In the cross-examination also they have admitted that the stick was not removed from the ice candy and they had purchased four kulfies from the accused but there is a clear breach of Rule 22.
The panch witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution and inspector also not clarified about obtaining training qua collecting the sample.

There was breach of Section 9(a) of the Act and samples were not sent within 7 days for the analyses and mandatory breach of provisions of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/560/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/03/2026 undefined Section 13(2) of the Act and Rule 14.
Even the sample is not properly sent for analysis.
Hence, requested to extend the benefit of amendment.

3) Learned APP for respondent - State has submitted that both the Courts have rightly convicted the applicant and as there is concurrent finding no interference of this Court is required and requested to dismiss the present application.

4) Having heard both the learned Advocates, at the outset, sample of ice candy was collected on 06.06.1995 and after analysis the accused had filed application for reanalysis of the sample and exercised his right under Section 13(2) of the Act and sample was sent to Ghaziyabad Laboratory for reanalysis.
If we consider the sample in the ice candy the fat and protein contents were found less and due to this reason the sample was found sub- standard.

Hence, once sample is found sub-standard without discussing further on merits and in view of provision of Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, and in light of the judgment in Nemi Chand v. State of Rajasthan, reported in (2018) 17 SCC 448, and Triloki Chand v. State of Himachal Pradesh, reported in (2020) 10 SCC 763, this Court is of the view that the applicant has already undergone 10 days sentence and paid Rs.1,000/- as fine and since concurrent finding is there, the sentence of six months simple imprisonment NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/560/2009 JUDGMENT DATED:
18/03/2026 undefined is modified to 10 days imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/- (One Thousand)
will serve the ends of justice.

sentences.text: 5) Accordingly, present revision application is partly allowed.

The judgment dated 30.04.1999 passed by the learned 2nd Joint Civil Judge & JMFC, Amreli in Criminal Case No.1603 of 1995, as well as judgment dated 31.08.2009 passed in Criminal Appeal No.7 of 1999, by the learned Sessions Judge, Amreli, are upheld.
However, the order of quantum of sentence is modified to 10 days imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000/- (One Thousand) upon the accused in lieu of simple imprisonment of six months.
